newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BANK SELL-OFF TENDER TO BE ANNOUNCED.
newsitem.headline: BANK SELL-OFF TENDER TO BE ANNOUNCED.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Wednesday that the privatisation tender for the State Commercial Bank will be announced next week.
"The documents for the bid, which includes the conditions and procedures, will be discussed with parliament's budget and finance committtee on Friday," Shemeta told a news conference.
"We intend to announce the tender next week and we will be expecting the applications to be submitted within a month from the date of the announcement," he added.
The huge State Commercial Bank is one of two state-run banks which the government has committed itself to delivering into private hands.
The bank had a staggering loss of over 170 million litas in 1996 which stemmed from a crippling portfolio of bad loans.
It was snatched from the brink of insolvency last summer by a fresh injection of 165 million litas in share capital from the government.
Despite its formidable problems, analysts say that the bank has a good branch network and could be a good investment - at the right price.
